content.text: Ask mode blocked the graph tools, so I’ll search the header/auth code directly.

The screenshot is doing exactly what the code currently does: **identity and the workspace CTA are one orange control**, and the label is the **email**. That comes from `Header` passing `showIdentity` into `AuthCta`, which then packs avatar + email + “Open workspace” into a single primary button: ```63:69:homepage/components/Header.tsx
``` ```72:88:homepage/components/AuthCta.tsx return ( ); ``` And `label` is email-first: ```13:15:homepage/lib/auth.ts export function authUserLabel(user: AuthUser): string { return user.email || user.username || "?"; } ``` That is why you see `A` + `a.mortezaie98@gm...` + `Open workspace` as one pill. ## Two separate problems **1. Layout.** One button is doing two jobs: “who am I” and “go to the board”. That makes the CTA look like a truncated account chip, not an action. **2. Data.** Google already stores a real name as `display_name` (from the `name` claim), but `/api/auth/status` never returns it: ```65:73:relocation_jobs/core/auth.py return { "authenticated": True, "user": { "id": user["id"], "username": user["username"], "email": user.get("email") or "", "is_admin": is_user_admin(user["id"]), "plan": user.get("plan") or "free", }, ``` So the homepage cannot show “Amin” even if it wanted to. `username` is just the email local part (`a.mortezaie98`), which is only slightly better than the full address. ## Recommended UI Signed-in header should be two elements, not one: `[A Amin]` `[Open workspace]` - **Identity** sits to the left of the CTA: avatar + first name, navy text on the white nav, **not** a button. Tooltip can still be the full email. - **Open workspace** stays the orange pill, action-only. No avatar, no email inside it. - Signed-out stays a single `Sign in` button. On small screens, hide the name and keep avatar + CTA so the bar does not overflow. That matches the screenshot: identity lives *next to* the action, not *inside* it. ## What to change | Layer | Change | |---|---| | `auth_status()` | Include `display_name` | | `AuthUser` + `fetchAuthStatus` | Accept `display_name` | | `authUserLabel` | Prefer `display_name` → first name; fallback `username` → email local part → email | | `AuthCta` / `Header` | Split identity chip from the workspace button | Label helper, roughly: ```ts export function authUserLabel(user: AuthUser): string { const name = user.display_name.trim(); if (name) return name.split(/\s+/)[0]; // "Amin Mortezaie" → "Amin" if (user.username) return user.username; const email = user.email.trim(); return email.includes("@") ? email.split("@")[0] : email || "?"; } ``` Header signed-in markup, roughly: ```tsx
{initial} {name}
``` Existing accounts already have `display_name` if they signed in with Google. If that column is empty, a re-login updates it via `touch_google_profile`. Until then, fall back to username so you never show the truncated Gmail string in the bar. I'm in Ask mode, so I cannot edit this. Switch to Agent mode if you want me to implement the split header and the `display_name` plumbing.
I'll split the header identity from the workspace button and wire `display_name` through auth status so the bar shows a name instead of the email.
